sentences.text:
On The 8 th Of April, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 14685 of 2025
 Rohit
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Anil Kumar Tiwari - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Ravindra Rajput- Panel Lawyer for the respondent/S
 Order

This is the second bail application under Section 483 of BNSS filed by the applicant for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.167/2024, registered at Police Station - Mundi, District-Khandwa (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366-A, 376 (3), 376(2)(n) of IPC and under Sections 5(L)/6 and 3/4(2) of POCSO Act.

Applicant is in detention since 06.06.2024.
2.
Earlier application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 19.03.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 8926/2025.
3. According to case of the prosecution, allegation against the applicant is that he abducted the minor prosecutrix and repeatedly committed sexual intercourse with her without her consent.
On the basis of report, FIR has been registered against the applicant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the offence.
It is further submitted that statements of the prosecutrix, mother and father have been recorded and they have not supported the prosecution story.
There is no criminal antecedents of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17176 2 MCRC-14685-2025 applicant.
Investigation is complete and charge-sheet has been filed.
Applicant is in jail since 06.06.2024.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail pending the trial.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the grant of bail to the applicant.
6. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that applicant be released on bail.

sentences.text: 1 Consequently, the bail application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of Cr.P.C.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
